How WebView, proxies, source-specified IPs and system DNS differ

Source-specified IPs and hosts take priority over domain rules, which in turn take priority over the feature switches.

Routing only controls native requests the app issues itself. Login pages, WebView sub-resources, template scripts and system or third-party TTS are not routed automatically. A proxy usually resolves the target domain; the app may only resolve the proxy server.

Benchmarks use the currently saved service and IPv6 setting, query the domain directly, and ignore hosts, routing and system fallback. DoH does not use the local HTTP cache; the first run includes connection setup and later runs may reuse it. System DNS caching is controlled by the system. The result is DNS query time, not download speed.

Network settings, hosts and Cronet apply after restart; benchmark results never switch providers automatically.
Exact domains win; wildcards match subdomains only. When the DoH switch is off, everything follows the system.
